Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/robots/liorbenhorin__lerobot_so101_teleop --backend fake (exit 0; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 run wD-072 and reviewed_by is null; no human reviewed or tested this package, and no hardware, Isaac Sim or Isaac Lab run was made. The card's family-config/GymnasiumDriver decision was used unchanged: native is the card's confirmed RockAStackSimpleEnvCfg (source/lerobot_so101_teleop/tasks/rock_a_stack/rock_a_stack_env_cfg.py:119), env_id is the registered Lerobot-So101-Teleop-Rock-A-Stack-Simple (source/lerobot_so101_teleop/tasks/rock_a_stack/__init__.py:9-16), and the driver serves cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1. The other three registered tasks (Base, Rock-A-Stack Hard and Rock-A-Stack Hard-Eval) are not served: one package serves one environment, and this is the README's run example (README.md:72-75). The card's mock_strategy.preferred is upstream-sim, but the simulator is Isaac Sim 5.1.0 with Isaac Lab v2.3.0 on Python 3.11 with a GPU (README.md:4-6, :38-47, source/lerobot_so101_teleop/pyproject.toml:12), none of which is installed where the gate runs; package code never imports the clone, so the fake backend is this package's pure-Python F0 kinematic stand-in and no sim backend was run. The fake models the contract the clone configures: six joint-position targets (base_env_cfg.py:141-146), the policy group with the joint positions and the visual group with camera_ego and camera_external (base_env_cfg.py:154-190), the 1/60 s policy step (decimation 2 at a 1/120 s simulation timestep, :294-305), the 5 s episode (:298) and no rewards or terminations (:290-291). NOT COVERED: the real 480 x 640 x 3 RGB camera arrays (base_env_cfg.py:75-80 and :105-110) - the fake returns 18 flat placeholder values per camera and the real size is stated in the fidelity gaps; rigid-body dynamics, contacts, actuators, sensors, rendering, the physics material and the Rock-A-Stack reset randomisation (rock_a_stack_env_cfg.py:66-135); the upstream environment is vectorised and returns torch tensors while the fake serves one environment with Python lists; the action space is published as an unbounded six-element Box because the clone configures the joint-position term and its scale but states no numeric bound, so no bound was invented, G8 awards CL2 and SAFE-014 has nothing to probe; the 300-step truncation is derived from the configured 5 s episode and was not observed upstream. Expected warnings, none a failure: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge only records the seed for the next reset); five G7.MAYBE_ABSENT for action_space, observation_space, reset, step and close (the card's native is the configuration class and the Gymnasium environment API comes from ManagerBasedRLEnv outside the clone); G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE and four G8.NO_UNIT for ticks, action.values and the two seed inputs, which the Gymnasium bridge derives without units. G4 reported no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings (all 26 Facts cite lines of the clone; show_refs.py reported 0 bad citations). No catalogue requests: only the card's three cap.world.* classes are used. No operator-required bound and no site-limits.example.json: the device is simulated R0. gate.digest is the digest line of the last gate run; check-report.json is regenerated by every run and is not part of the package.
